questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I think my biggest motivation was the opportunity to move to and live in another country and city and create every day life here. So a mix between trying another uni/academic opportunities and new cultures.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really found the courses at UvA interesting. And also that I haven't been in Amsterdam or the Netherlands before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Of course it has been hard sometimes and I was surprised how much time I ended up using at the university, but I also found it really interesting and I feel that I have learned a lot! Being on exchange is a busy time with uni, friends and exploring and overall I feel that it ended up being much better than expected (even though I don't really know what I expected).

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think UvA was really good at providing information and you always knew who to contact or ask if needed. So I think it was quite easy!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A got a lot of e-mails from the university - both before arrival and after arrival. The mails contained a lot of information about what steps should be done etc. They also hosted intro-meetings after arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
The university has some arrangements with some housing companies. When you sign up for this you will get a mail whether they are able to offer you a room or not. Then, you will be able to choose from a list. 

I would recommend to sign up for student accommodation/housing (even though you have to pay a fee) since it is very difficult to find housing in Amsterdam.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The place I lived was pretty near campus and also student accommodation. It was nice it was close since the way to uni wasn't that long, however it was also nice it wasn't ON campus. Go explore the city outside campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You add the courses you want to a list divided on the different blocks (three blocks). You can choose courses that total 42 ECTS points - this is a good idea even though you only need 30 ECTS points since uni can't guarantee that you get all the courses you want/wished for. I ended up getting all courses so I deregistered the two courses I wanted the least and ended on 30 ECTS points:)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Uni hosts an online info-meeting before course registration and you can also find information on their website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting all courses I wanted - I even had to deregister a few. I found it pretty easy and it ended being a success.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Add a few more courses than you need to the list to make sure you will get enough courses - you can always deregister again.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was fine. I think we learn a bit more classical theory and methodology at UCPH. On the other hand I think they are a bit better to discuss and to be more 'modern' and address modern crises in the courses at UvA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found it quite different from UCPH. Of course we had lectures which were similar - however participation is more common and also more a part of the lectures than what I was used to. I had tutorials to every course (I was not used to that) and the teaching style was more discussing, 'playing' etc. The final grade also consists of different grades you got through different presentations or assignments throughout the course - so a bit more performance I would say.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Rethinking Sustainable Societies: New Perspectives (Course catalogue number 5512SSPB6Y), 6 ETCS points
Love-Politics: Relationality, Futurity and Affect (Course catalogue number 7303S4004Y), 12 ECTS points
Circular Economy (Course catalogue number 5512CIEC6Y), 6 ECTS points
Degrowth (Course catalogue number 5512DEGR6Y), 6 ECTS points

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Circular Economy! Also Degrowth and Rethinking Sustainable Societies: New Perspectives. They were all interdisciplinary which was really interesting and fun to try!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Maybe I thought that grocery shopping would be a bit more cheap (as in Germany) - still cheaper than Denmark. Maybe I also experienced that I went out to drink coffee (and wine) more than I do at home (since it is cheaper). And also just a nice way to meet up with new friends:)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee and wine is extremely cheap compared to Denmark!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Both creative activities and student athletics are available. At campus they also have some cafes. Some museums, cinemas etc. also have a students discount.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visit some of the many museums, go to the cinema and explore the nice and cheap cafes and bars in Amsterdam.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In addition to go exploring Amsterdam I really enjoyed going on day- or weekend trips to other cities (Utrecht and Rotterdam) and also Belgium. It is very easy with the train and the FlixBus and not very far.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Amsterdam and Dutch culture in general are maybe not that different from Copenhagen and Danish culture. However, the Dutch people is maybe a bit more direct and less service minded. I also think there is some more competition and performance culture among students - even though they also do a lot of group work at uni.

In addition, Amsterdam is very international and a lot of international students go to UvA. It makes it easy to adjust in a way.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you feel a good vibe with someone just ask if they want to grab coffee - or if you should do group work together. I feel like other students are curios about your home country as well and find it interesting to hear about exchange etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I missed rye bread a lot!! It rains A LOT. Sometimes the directness is a bit much. Bike helmets are NOT a thing at all - not even for children.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cheap coffee and wine:) The directness and openness were also nice (sometimes the directness was a bit much). I also appreciate the biking culture (even though I think we are better at biking more safely in Denmark).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. There will be more assignments during the semester and you will maybe use a bit more time at uni than expected - but you will also be reading interesting stuff! (of course it also depends on who you are) I used the reading room at the library at campus a lot.
2. Go to the intro-week (even though the program is a bit weird) - it is a nice way to meet people! 
3. There is a lot of things to do all the time - use the city. Also remember it is totally fair to feel the need to be alone and 'stand down' sometimes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The staff at uni is very helpful - use them if you have questions.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think I have learned a lot - both at uni-level but also personally. Also very exciting to meet people from all over the world!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To overcome linguistic insecurities - in the beginning I really tried to think every sentence I wanted to say in English through in my head. After a month I feel like this changed at I felt more relaxed and just talked.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
